name: Okihiro Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Okihiro Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of Duane anomaly characterized by limited horizontal eye movement with globe retraction
Radial ray malformations including hypoplasia or aplasia of the thumb and/or radius
Craniofacial dysmorphisms such as downslanting palpebral fissures and ptosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both Duane anomaly and radial ray malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SALL4 mutations supports diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Duane anomaly with limited horizontal eye movement and globe retraction
searchTerms: eye muscle abnormality with globe retraction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radial ray malformations including thumb hypoplasia or aplasia

searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve or ear problems
difficulty hearing due to inner or middle ear issues

common.symptomName: Short forearms due to radius hypoplasia

searchTerms: holes or defects in heart walls

rare.symptomName: Renal anomalies such as unilateral renal agenesis

imaging: Radiographs showing radial ray defects and hypoplastic or absent radius
MRI or CT confirming Duane anomaly with absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve
genetic: Heterozygous mutations in the SALL4 gene on chromosome 20q13
other: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural or conductive hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Duane anomaly without radial ray malformations
Limb defects with different pattern and absence of Duane anomaly

redFlags: Severe radial aplasia leading to functional impairment
Cardiac septal defects causing heart failure symptoms
references: Okihiro MM et al. Duane-radial ray syndrome: a dominantly inherited disorder with upper limb and ocular anomalies. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
Al-Baradie R et al. Duane radial ray syndrome (Okihiro syndrome) maps to 20q13 and results from mutations in SALL4, a new member of the SAL family. Am J Hum Genet. 2002.
Orphanet: Okihiro syndrome. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
